```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

#uncomment if the libraries has not been installed before

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Data collection

```{r data_input}
coffee <- read_csv('../data/coffee_survey.csv', show_col_types = FALSE)
coffee$cups = as.factor(coffee$cups)
coffee$strength = as.factor(coffee$strength)
```


# Data Preprocessing

```{r column_choice_for_visualization}
cols = c('age','total_spend','gender', 'education_level')
```

We want to remove NA values so that we just look at the data that is complete.To justify this we need to see what percentage of our data will be left over if we decide to do this.

```{r na_value_inspection}
paste("Missing data %:",round((nrow(coffee[cols])-nrow(na.omit(coffee[cols])))/nrow(coffee[cols])*100,2))
paste("Leftover samples: ",nrow(na.omit(coffee[cols])))
```

We are removing 16.3% of the data, but we will still have 3383 of the 4042 samples. This is acceptable.

```{r create_clean_dataframe}
coffee_no_na <- na.omit(coffee[cols])
```


```{r}
head(coffee_no_na)

```

```{r}
age_levels <- c(
  "<18 years old",
  "18-24 years old",
  "25-34 years old",
  "35-44 years old",
  "45-54 years old",
  "55-64 years old",
  ">65 years old"
)

# Prepare data: keep only the three gender categories
coffee_processed <- coffee_no_na %>%
  filter(gender %in% c("Male", "Female", "Non-binary")) %>%
  mutate(
    total_spend_numeric = case_when(
      total_spend == "<$20" ~ 10,
      total_spend == "$20-$40" ~ 30,
      total_spend == "$40-$60" ~ 50,
      total_spend == "$60-$80" ~ 70,
      total_spend == "$80-$100" ~ 90,
      total_spend == ">$100" ~ 110,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    age = factor(age, levels = age_levels),
    gender_group = factor(
      gender,
      levels = c("Male", "Female", "Non-binary")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(age),
    !is.na(total_spend_numeric)
  )

# Calculate mean spending by age and gender
age_gender_mean <- coffee_processed %>%
  group_by(age, gender_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_spend = mean(total_spend_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Define colors
gender_colors <- c(
  "Male" = "lightblue",
  "Female" = "pink",
  "Non-binary" = "purple"
)

# Plot
ggplot(
  age_gender_mean,
  aes(
    x = age,
    y = mean_spend,
    fill = gender_group
  )
) +
  # Dashed separators between age groups
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = seq(1.5, length(age_levels) - 0.5, by = 1),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray60",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.85),
    width = 0.75
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = gender_colors,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Coffee Spending by Age Group and Gender",
    x = "Age Group",
    y = "Mean Spending per Respondent ($)",
    fill = "Gender"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```


```{r}
# Calculate average spending by age and education level
age_education_average <- coffee_processed %>%
  group_by(age, education_level) %>%
  summarise(
    average_spending = mean(total_spend_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot average spending
ggplot(
  age_education_average,
  aes(
    x = age,
    y = average_spending,
    color = education_level,
    group = education_level
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Coffee Spending by Age and Education",
    x = "Age Group",
    y = "Mean Coffee Spending per Person ($)",
    color = "Education Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```


```{r}
# Calculate average spending by age and education level
age_education_average <- coffee_processed %>%
  group_by(age, education_level) %>%
  summarise(
    average_spending = mean(total_spend_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    highlighted = ifelse(
      education_level == "Doctorate or professional degree",
      "Doctorate or professional degree",
      "Other Education Levels"
    )
  )

# Plot average spending, highlighting doctorate/professional degree
ggplot(
  age_education_average,
  aes(
    x = age,
    y = average_spending,
    group = education_level,
    color = highlighted
  )
) +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = highlighted), alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(size = highlighted)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Doctorate or professional degree" = "purple",
      "Other Education Levels" = "gray70"
    )
  ) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(
    values = c(
      "Doctorate or professional degree" = 1.4,
      "Other Education Levels" = 0.7
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_size_manual(
    values = c(
      "Doctorate or professional degree" = 3,
      "Other Education Levels" = 1.8
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Coffee Spending by Age and Education",
    subtitle = "Doctorate or professional degree highlighted",
    x = "Age Group",
    y = "Mean Coffee Spending per Person ($)",
    color = "Education Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```
